messages:
alex_k: Quick heads-up — after landing the kernel-selection tweak that biases toward fused attention kernels were seeing a 6-12% host-side p50 increase on short streaming requests. Repro: small prompt (<=64 tokens) over gRPC streaming to ingress. gist: https://redwood/gists/ingress-kernel-bench

maria_s: ack. I ran a microbench on canary nodes this morning. p50 up ~8%, p95 up ~15% for 32-token samples. CPU profiles point at extra syscall/writev churn in the grpc write path.

raj_p: interesting — did the kernel change alter output chunking sizes or KV cache hit alignment? small kernel latencies can shift request pacing and cause more small write()s.

jen_w: I grabbed a flamegraph and the hotspot is in host-side framing + socket write path. stack shows repeated calls to grpc::Call::Write with ~128-256B payloads more often than before. Suspect chunk boundary drift.

perf-bot: auto-bench summary (canary vs main, median of 1000 runs):
- main (pre-change): p50=42ms p95=120ms avg_writev_calls=3
- canary (post-change): p50=46ms p95=138ms avg_writev_calls=6

alex_k: thanks. so we have two hypotheses: (1) kernel selection changed emission pacing -> more fragmentation at ingress, (2) batching/auto-coalesce heuristics need to account for changed token latency distribution.

maria_s: i instrumented kv-cache metrics during runs. KV hit-rate unchanged but there are more short-lived KV fetches per request (micro-bursts). might be because decoder loop now yields more frequently.

jen_w: dump from ingress tcp stats and writev trace: ```
[INFO] writes: 6 per stream
[INFO] avg_write_size: 200B
[DEBUG] last_chunk_sizes: [120, 80, 200, 160, 88, 32]
```

raj_p: that pattern looks like misaligned chunk stitching. Proposed quick triage: enable adaptive chunk coalescing on ingress (delay up to 2ms to accumulate small writes) + add a kernel-selection hint to prefer slightly larger decode micro-batches for streaming small prompts.

alex_k: agree on coalescing as a quick mitigation. downside: adds small latency tail for very-low-latency usecases. we should make it an opt-in runtime flag and default on canary. Also add a metric: "grpc_small_write_count" and expose in console.

maria_s: i'll prepare a canary config: ingress.coalesce_window_ms=2, ingress.writev_threshold=512, runtime.kernel_hint=streaming_bias_low_latency:0.8. will run 10k sample sweep.

jen_w: also suggest bumping the batching heuristic so that when per-token decode < X ms we increase minibatch target by 1 for N steps to reduce churn. pseudocode: ```if avg_token_latency < 0.5ms: target_batch += 1 for next 20 steps```

perf-bot: canary run queued. estimated completion 40m. baseline/regression alerts suppressed for this thread. :hourglass_flowing_sand: 

alex_k: action items:
- maria: push canary config + run sweep and attach raw traces (due EOD)
- jen: add grpc_small_write_count + writev size histogram to console (due tomorrow)
- raj: prototype kernel-selection hint toggle and test effect on micro-batching (PTA)

raj_p: quick question — do we have automation to roll back kernel hint if downstream quality/regression is observed?

alex_k: yes, rollout uses canary + auto-fallback to model-compat variant. we'll gate full rollout until we verify no quality regressions.

maria_s: posting initial canary summary in 30m. thanks all :thumbsup:

jen_w: one more note — watch gRPC keepalive/backpressure flags. if the socket buffers saturate we'll see large tail spikes. worth adding a small probe in ingress to log socket buffer occupancy on high-churn streams.
